forces.title: Surging AI-driven demand for semiconductors transforms market growth
forces.description: The rise of AI is responsible for an unprecedented surge in the semiconductor market. Major hyperscalers are committing vast capital expenditures for AI infrastructure, directly fueling demand for leading-edge chips and memory. This strong, sustained demand is pushing up average selling prices (ASPs) and is expected to drive the global semiconductor market to $2.3 trillion by 2030, marking a shift from cyclical to sustained growth patterns.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Value shifts to leading-edge chips and HBM as core growth engines
forces.description: The semiconductor industry is undergoing a structural shift where leading-edge nodes (7nm or less) and High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) are becoming the twin engines of growth. AI applications are accelerating demand for these advanced components, leading to a rare scenario where both volume and Average Selling Prices (ASPs) are increasing. This fundamental change in demand drivers is permanently reshaping industry economics, favoring companies focused on these high-value segments.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Elevated Average Selling Prices (ASPs) persist for advanced semiconductors
forces.description: Unlike historical patterns of decline, Average Selling Prices (ASPs) for leading-edge chips (e.g., 3nm, 5nm) are increasing by 2% or more annually, and DRAM prices have surged sixfold since early 2023. This is primarily driven by strong, AI-induced demand coupled with limited manufacturing capacity. These persistently high ASPs provide a significant tailwind to revenue growth for semiconductor design and fabrication firms, improving profitability and overall market value.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Persistent supply-demand imbalance constrains advanced chip availability
forces.description: Despite significant investments in capacity, the current supply shortage for leading-edge chips (7nm or less) and High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) is expected to persist for at least three to five more years. This imbalance, while supporting high ASPs, acts as a bottleneck, potentially limiting the overall volume of chips that can be designed and fabricated to meet surging AI-driven demand, thereby constraining total market growth potential.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Energy availability and affordability challenge European data center build-out
forces.description: AI data centers are highly energy-intensive, and meeting their power demands through 2030 requires overcoming significant constraints, including cost-related ones. The report notes that Europe 'may lag other regions' in addressing these energy challenges. This poses a headwind to the necessary AI infrastructure build-out in Europe, which in turn could dampen local demand for semiconductors, impacting the region's semiconductor design and fabrication sector.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Innovation in AI ecosystem accelerates chip demand through cost reduction
forces.description: To broaden AI adoption and sustain high demand for semiconductors, the costs of AI inference must drop significantly. Innovation roadmaps in networking, photonics, memory, software, and algorithms are making this reduction more feasible. Such advancements will lower the barrier to entry for AI applications, consequently driving further and broader adoption of AI, acting as a significant upside driver for semiconductor demand and design.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

viewpoints.title: AI fuels unprecedented semiconductor growth, reshaping industry dynamics permanently
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that AI is driving an unprecedented surge in the semiconductor sector, with sales reaching a 40-year high. Hyperscalers' substantial AI infrastructure investments are pushing up average selling prices (ASPs) for leading-edge chips and memory. This macro-trend is projected to expand the global market to $2.3 trillion by 2030, a 44% increase from prior estimates, suggesting a structural shift from cyclical to sustained growth, which will significantly benefit semiconductor design and fabrication companies.
viewpoints.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: Five major hyperscalers are planning cumulative capital expenditures of $800 billion for 2026 and $1 trillion for 2027, with the vast majority directed toward AI infrastructure, significantly boosting demand for chips.
The proliferation of data centers, driven by AI, is a primary factor sustaining high demand for semiconductors, especially leading-edge chips and memory.
AI models require large amounts of memory (DRAM, HBM) to store parameters and process data rapidly, with requirements increasing with context window size, concurrent users, and token volume.

pnl_drivers.description: Strong demand from AI and limited supply for leading-edge chips (7nm or less) and memory (HBM, DRAM) are driving ASPs significantly higher than historical patterns, boosting revenue per chip.

new_opportunities.description: Companies are investing in new fabrication facilities to increase DRAM and HBM manufacturing capacity, addressing supply shortages and capturing future demand.
Exploring advanced packaging (e.g., taller HBM stacks, 2.5D or 3D integration) to increase memory density and bandwidth is a key avenue for innovation and value creation.
Developing next-generation technology to increase the bit density per wafer for DRAM offers an opportunity to enhance memory supply and performance.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Increased Bit Density per Wafer for DRAM

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey's base case projection for the global semiconductor market value, derived from a comprehensive look at value generated by fabless companies, OEMs with in-house design, and captive-chip players, factoring in strong AI-driven demand and increased Average Selling Prices (ASPs) for leading-edge chips and memory. The range is $1.7 trillion to $2.6 trillion.
market_sizing.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: The rapid expansion of AI data centers is the primary demand driver for server and data center chips, including specialized AI compute.

pnl_drivers.description: An intensifying supply-demand imbalance in the server and data center segment contributes to higher ASPs, boosting revenue growth.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecast for global chip sales revenue specifically for servers and data centers. The figure is projected to rise from $330 billion in 2025 to $1.2 trillion by 2030.
market_sizing.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: Strong demand from AI and high-performance computing applications is a key driver for the value growth of leading-edge chips.

pnl_drivers.description: Unlike historical patterns of decline, ASPs for 3nm and 5nm wafers are increasing due to strong demand and limited capacity, directly enhancing value.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected value increase for leading-edge chips (7 nanometers or less), driven by significant increases in Average Selling Prices (ASPs), combined with volume and mix effects. ASPs for 3nm and 5nm wafers are increasing by 2% or more annually.
market_sizing.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: AI models necessitate vast amounts of memory to store parameters and process data rapidly, with HBM providing crucial bandwidth for efficient compute resources.

pnl_drivers.description: DRAM prices have increased roughly sixfold since early 2023 due to surging AI demand and limited supply, significantly boosting memory segment revenues.
Despite potential declines due to increased competition, HBM is expected to maintain attractive merchant gross margins, supporting segment profitability.

new_opportunities.description: Investing in new fabs to increase DRAM and HBM manufacturing capacity is a long-term solution to address supply shortages and capture demand.
Exploring advanced packaging solutions like taller HBM stacks and 2.5D/3D integration can increase memory density and bandwidth.
Increasing bit density per wafer for DRAM through next-generation technology offers an opportunity to improve supply efficiency.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected value increase for memory (especially DRAM and High-Bandwidth Memory - HBM), based on rising demand from AI models and significant increases in ASPs. Merchant gross margins for HBM are expected to remain attractive despite competitive pressures.
market_sizing.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story
